function cloneQ(q){return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(q))}
function uniqueById(arr){const m=new Map();arr.forEach(q=>q&&m.set(q.id,q));return [...m.values()]}
/* v58: the dedup key used to stringify `choices` in its ORIGINAL order and
 * key on the correct-answer INDEX rather than its actual text — so the same
 * question regenerated with its choices shuffled into a different order (a
 * real, confirmed pattern: 338 SAT and 423 ACT question-instances were exact
 * content dupes of another item, differing only in choice order/id) produced
 * a different key each time and slipped through as if it were new content,
 * contradicting this project's own "100% unique by content" claim. Sorting
 * the choices before hashing, and keying on the correct choice's TEXT
 * instead of its index, makes the key order-independent while still telling
 * genuinely different questions (different wording or different correct
 * answer) apart.
 *
 * A follow-up audit found 6 SAT "line slope" pairs (e.g. SAT-B1M-ALG-01 /
 * SAT-ENR-0628) that were still slipping through: one generator wrote the
 * minus sign as U+2212 ("−") and the other as a plain hyphen ("-"), so two
 * choice sets that were textually identical to a reader hashed to different
 * keys. dashNorm() folds every dash/minus lookalike (and whitespace/case) to
 * one form before the key is built, so this class of near-duplicate can't
 * slip through again. */
function dashNorm(s){return String(s==null?'':s).replace(/[‐-―−]/g,'-').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().toLowerCase()}
function uniqueByContent(arr){const m=new Map();arr.forEach(q=>{if(!q)return;const choices=q.choices||[];const correctText=choices[q.a]!==undefined?choices[q.a]:q.a;const key=dashNorm(q.section)+'|'+dashNorm(q.passage)+'|'+dashNorm(q.q)+'|'+JSON.stringify([...choices].map(dashNorm).sort())+'|'+dashNorm(correctText);if(!m.has(key))m.set(key,q);});return [...m.values()]}
function pct(c,t){return t?Math.round(c/t*100):0}

occur everywhere.'],a:0,ex:infer,why:['Best-supported inference.','Contradicted by the passage.','Contradicted by the described response or result.','Overgeneralizes beyond the function v17pick(a,i){return a[Math.abs(i)%a.length]}
function v17diff(i){return i%5===0?'Hard':i%2===0?'Medium':'Easy'}
/* Used only for confirmed single/two-step arithmetic and algebra templates
 * (simple one-variable equations, one-formula geometry, one percent step) —
 * v17diff's index-based "some fraction are Hard regardless of content" isn't
 * honest for these, since none of them actually get harder at any index.
 * Genuinely multi-step Math templates (systems of equations, multi-step
 * probability) keep their own difficulty logic rather than using this. */
function v17mathDiff(i){return i%3===0?'Easy':'Medium'}
function v17uniqChoices(vals){return new Set(vals.map(String)).size===vals.length}
function v17numChoices(correct,i,step=1){let vals=[correct,correct+step,correct-step,correct+2*step];if(!v17uniqChoices(vals)) vals=[correct,correct+1,correct+2,correct+3];return vals.map(v=>Number.isInteger(v)?String(v):String(+v.toFixed(2)))}

 if(k===5){const vals=[12+j%7,14+j%7,16+j%7,18+j%7],mean=vals.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/4;return{id:`SAT-V17-M-STAT-${i}`,section:'Math',skill:'Problem-Solving & Data Analysis',difficulty:'Easy',calculatorAllowed:true,q:`The values are ${vals.join(', ')}. function v17Fill(exam,target,maker){let i=0,guard=0;while(PRO_BANK[exam].length<target&&guard<target*5){const q=maker(i++);if(q&&!PRO_BANK[exam].some(x=>x.id===q.id))PRO_BANK[exam].push(q);guard++}}
v17Fill('SAT',V17_TARGETS.SAT,v17SATOne);v17Fill('ACT',V17_TARGETS.ACT,v17ACTOne);v17Fill('TSIA2',V17_TARGETS.TSIA2,v17TSIOne);
function v17BalanceAnswerPositions(bank){
  bank.forEach((q,idx)=>{
    if(!q||!Array.isArray(q.choices)||q.choices.length!==4||!Array.isArray(q.why)||q.why.length!==4)return;
    const shift=idx%4;
    if(!shift)return;
    const items=q.choices.map((choice,i)=>({choice,why:q.why[i],correct:i===q.a}));
    const rotated=items.slice(-shift).concat(items.slice(0,-shift));
    q.choices=rotated.map(x=>x.choice);q.why=rotated.map(x=>x.why);q.a=rotated.findIndex(x=>x.correct);
  });
}
v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.SAT);v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.ACT);v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.TSIA2);

function v17QualityAudit(bank,exam){const issues=[];const ids=new Set();for(const q of bank){if(!q||!q.id||ids.has(q.id)){issues.push([q?.id,'duplicate/missing id']);continue}ids.add(q.id);if(!q.section||!q.skill||!['Easy','Medium','Hard'].includes(q.difficulty))issues.push([q.id,'metadata']);if(!q.q||!Array.isArray(q.choices)||q.choices.length!==4||new Set(q.choices.map(String)).size!==4)issues.push([q.id,'choices']);if(!Number.isInteger(q.a)||q.a<0||q.a>3)issues.push([q.id,'answer']);if(!q.ex||q.ex.length<12)issues.push([q.id,'explanation']);if(!Array.isArray(q.why)||q.why.length!==4||q.why.some(x=>!x||x.length<3))issues.push([q.id,'why']);if(!q.strategy||q.strategy.length<8)issues.push([q.id,'strategy']);}return issues}
const V17_AUDIT={SAT:v17QualityAudit(PRO_BANK.SAT,'SAT'),ACT:v17QualityAudit(PRO_BANK.ACT,'ACT'),TSIA2:v17QualityAudit(PRO_BANK.TSIA2,'TSIA2')};
window.SCOREPATH_V17_BANK_REPORT={targets:V17_TARGETS,counts:{SAT:PRO_BANK.SAT.length,ACT:PRO_BANK.ACT.length,TSIA2:PRO_BANK.TSIA2.length,total:PRO_BANK.SAT.length+PRO_BANK.ACT.length+PRO_BANK.TSIA2.length},structuralIssues:{SAT:V17_AUDIT.SAT.length,ACT:V17_AUDIT.ACT.length,TSIA2:V17_AUDIT.TSIA2.length},note:'Original blueprint-aligned practice. Correct-answer positions are balanced in the bank and randomized again per student session. No previously administered official question is copied or lightly edited.'};
spConsole('info','TSI Practice Prep V17 5K bank',window.SCOREPATH_V17_BANK_REPORT);


/* ---------- V6: official-blueprint alignment + new high-fidelity ORIGINAL practice ---------- */
const SCOREPATH_BLUEPRINT={
 SAT:{
  sections:['Reading & Writing','Math'],
  domains:['Information & Ideas','Craft & Structure','Expression of Ideas','Standard English Conventions','Algebra','Advanced Math','Problem-Solving & Data Analysis','Geometry & Trigonometry']
 },
 ACT:{
  sections:['English','Math','Reading','Science (Optional)'],
  domains:['Production of Writing','Knowledge of Language','Conventions of Standard English','Number & Quantity','Algebra','Functions','Geometry','Statistics & Probability','Integrating Essential Skills','Modeling','Key Ideas & Details','Craft & Structure','Integration of Knowledge & Ideas','Interpretation of Data','Scientific Investigation','Evaluating Scientific Arguments and Models with Evidence']
 },
 TSIA2:{
  sections:['Mathematics','ELAR'],
  domains:['Quantitative Reasoning','Algebraic Reasoning','Geometric and Spatial Reasoning','Probabilistic and Statistical Reasoning','Literary Text Analysis','Informational Text Analysis and Synthesis','Essay Revision and Editing','Sentence Revision, Editing, and Completion']
 }
};
function blueprintDomain(exam,q){
 const s=q.skill||'',sec=q.section||'';
 if(exam==='SAT') return SCOREPATH_BLUEPRINT.SAT.domains.includes(s)?s:null;
 if(exam==='ACT'){
  if(sec==='English'){
   if(/Organization|Rhetoric|Production/i.test(s))return 'Production of Writing';
   if(/Language|Style|Conciseness|Word Choice/i.test(s))return 'Knowledge of Language';
   if(/Grammar|Usage|Punctuation|Conventions/i.test(s))return 'Conventions of Standard English';
  }
  if(sec==='Math'){
   if(/Number|Quantity/i.test(s))return 'Number & Quantity';
   if(/Algebra/i.test(s))return 'Algebra';
   if(/Function/i.test(s))return 'Functions';
   if(/Geometry|Trig/i.test(s))return 'Geometry';
   if(/Statistic|Probability/i.test(s))return 'Statistics & Probability';
   if(/Integrating|Essential/i.test(s))return 'Integrating Essential Skills';
   if(/Model/i.test(s))return 'Modeling';
  }
  if(sec==='Reading'){
   if(/Main Idea|Inference|Key Ideas|Detail/i.test(s))return 'Key Ideas & Details';
   if(/Craft|Structure|Vocabulary|Author/i.test(s))return 'Craft & Structure';
   if(/Integration|Knowledge|Evidence/i.test(s))return 'Integration of Knowledge & Ideas';
  }
  if(sec==='Science (Optional)'){
   if(/Data|Interpret/i.test(s))return 'Interpretation of Data';
   if(/Experiment|Investigation|Design/i.test(s))return 'Scientific Investigation';
   if(/Model|Inference|Argument|Evidence/i.test(s))return 'Evaluating Scientific Arguments and Models with Evidence';
  }
  return null;
 }
 if(exam==='TSIA2'){
  if(sec==='Mathematics'){
   if(/Quantitative/i.test(s))return 'Quantitative Reasoning';
   if(/Algebraic/i.test(s))return 'Algebraic Reasoning';
   if(/Geometric|Spatial/i.test(s))return 'Geometric and Spatial Reasoning';
   if(/Probabilistic|Statistical/i.test(s))return 'Probabilistic and Statistical Reasoning';
  }
  if(sec==='ELAR'){
   if(/Literary/i.test(s))return 'Literary Text Analysis';
   if(/Main Idea|Inference|Vocabulary|Author|Informational/i.test(s))return 'Informational Text Analysis and Synthesis';
   if(/Revision|Organization/i.test(s))return 'Essay Revision and Editing';
   if(/Sentence|Grammar|Usage|Editing|Transition/i.test(s))return 'Sentence Revision, Editing, and Completion';
  }
  return null;
 }
 return null;
}
function validatePracticeItem(exam,q){
 const bp=SCOREPATH_BLUEPRINT[exam];
 if(!q||!bp||!bp.sections.includes(q.section))return false;
 if(!Array.isArray(q.choices)||q.choices.length!==4||!Number.isInteger(q.a)||q.a<0||q.a>3)return false;
 if(!q.q||!q.ex||!Array.isArray(q.why)||q.why.length!==4||!q.strategy)return false;
 const d=blueprintDomain(exam,q);if(!d)return false;
 q.blueprintDomain=d;q.contentOrigin='TSI Practice Prep original — official-blueprint aligned';q.blueprintVerified=true;
 return true;
}
function O(id,section,skill,difficulty,q,choices,a,ex,why,strategy,extra={}){return {id,section,skill,difficulty,q,choices,a,ex,why,strategy,...extra}}

/* ---------- Full Digital SAT adaptive controller ---------- */
let satAdaptive=null;
/* Fifty-ninth pass: routeLabel used to always compare against a hardcoded 70,
 * even where the caller's actual routing decision used a different threshold
 * (TSIA2's Module 2 routing below uses 60) — a TSIA2 student scoring 60-69%
 * was actually routed into the harder Module 2 while this label displayed
 * "Foundational/Mixed Route", the opposite of what happened. routeLabel now
 * takes the threshold the caller actually routed on, so the label always
 * matches the real routing decision. Defaults to SAT_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD for
 * existing SAT call sites that don't pass one explicitly. */
function routeLabel(acc,threshold=SAT_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD){return acc>=threshold?'Higher-Difficulty Route':'Foundational/Mixed Route'}
/* ---------- V22: blueprint-proportional sampling for full/adaptive test modules ----------
 * Domain-weight approximations, checked against primary sources (not guessed):
 * - SAT Reading & Writing / Math: College Board, "Assessment Framework for
 *   the Digital SAT Suite" v3.01 (Aug 2024), Tables 10 & 16 — College Board's
 *   own figures are printed with "≈", i.e. these are official approximate
 *   splits, not exact integer percentages.
 * - ACT (current Enhanced ACT, 2025+): ACT Education Corp., "Comparison of
 *   the Legacy and Enhanced ACT Test Total Test and Reporting Categories"
 *   (MR038103, 2025) — midpoints of ACT's own published Enhanced-ACT ranges.
 *   Math's cross-cutting "Modeling" category is intentionally left out of
 *   this split: ACT's own document describes Modeling items as also
 *   counting toward one of the other Math categories, not a separate slice.
 * - TSIA2 Mathematics / ELAR: THECB/College Board, "TSIA2 Mathematics Test
 *   Specifications" and "TSIA2 ELAR Test Specifications", v1.4 (Jan 2021) —
 *   the CRC-form's own official item counts per domain (exact, not derived).
 * These weights only shape how TSI Practice Prep samples its OWN original practice
 * questions across the domains it already tags each item with
 * (blueprintDomain, above) — they never affect scoring and are never used
 * to claim or imply an official score. */
const SCOREPATH_BLUEPRINT_WEIGHTS={
 SAT:{
  'Reading & Writing':{'Information & Ideas':.26,'Craft & Structure':.28,'Expression of Ideas':.20,'Standard English Conventions':.26},
  'Math':{'Algebra':.35,'Advanced Math':.35,'Problem-Solving & Data Analysis':.15,'Geometry & Trigonometry':.15}
 },
 ACT:{
  'English':{'Production of Writing':.40,'Knowledge of Language':.20,'Conventions of Standard English':.40},
  'Math':{'Number & Quantity':.11,'Algebra':.19,'Functions':.19,'Geometry':.19,'Statistics & Probability':.13,'Integrating Essential Skills':.19},
  'Reading':{'Key Ideas & Details':.48,'Craft & Structure':.30,'Integration of Knowledge & Ideas':.22},
  'Science (Optional)':{'Interpretation of Data':.42,'Scientific Investigation':.24,'Evaluating Scientific Arguments and Models with Evidence':.34}
 },
 TSIA2:{
  'Mathematics':{'Quantitative Reasoning':.30,'Algebraic Reasoning':.35,'Geometric and Spatial Reasoning':.15,'Probabilistic and Statistical Reasoning':.20},
  'ELAR':{'Literary Text Analysis':.133,'Informational Text Analysis and Synthesis':.367,'Essay Revision and Editing':.133,'Sentence Revision, Editing, and Completion':.367}
 }
};
/* Largest-remainder rounding: turns fractional weight*count targets into
 * whole-number per-domain counts that always sum to exactly `count`. */
function domainTargetCounts(examKey,section,count){
 const weights=(SCOREPATH_BLUEPRINT_WEIGHTS[examKey]||{})[section];
 if(!weights)return null;
 const rows=Object.keys(weights).map(d=>({d,exact:count*weights[d]}));
 const targets={};let assigned=0;
 rows.forEach(r=>{targets[r.d]=Math.floor(r.exact);assigned+=targets[r.d]});
 let remainder=count-assigned;
 rows.sort((a,b)=>(b.exact-Math.floor(b.exact))-(a.exact-Math.floor(a.exact)));
 for(let i=0;i<remainder&&rows.length;i++)targets[rows[i%rows.length].d]++;
 return targets;
}
function pickByDifficulty(pool,count,weights){
 let picked=[];
 for(const d of ['Easy','Medium','Hard']){const want=Math.round(count*weights[d]);picked.push(...secureShuffle(pool.filter(q=>q.difficulty===d&&!picked.includes(q))).slice(0,want))}
 if(picked.length<count)picked.push(...secureShuffle(pool.filter(q=>!picked.includes(q))).slice(0,count-picked.length));
 return picked.slice(0,count);
}
function adaptivePick(pool,count,route,used,examKey,section){
 const available=pool.filter(q=>!used.has(q.id));
 const diffWeights=route==='hard'?{Easy:.15,Medium:.4,Hard:.45}:route==='foundation'?{Easy:.48,Medium:.4,Hard:.12}:{Easy:.3,Medium:.45,Hard:.25};
 const targets=(examKey&&section)?domainTargetCounts(examKey,section,count):null;
 let picked=[];
 if(targets){
  const byDomain={};Object.keys(targets).forEach(d=>byDomain[d]=[]);
  available.forEach(q=>{const d=blueprintDomain(examKey,q);if(d&&byDomain[d])byDomain[d].push(q)});
  Object.keys(targets).forEach(d=>{const got=pickByDifficulty(byDomain[d],targets[d],diffWeights);picked.push(...got.filter(q=>!picked.includes(q)))});
  if(picked.length<count){const leftover=available.filter(q=>!picked.includes(q));picked.push(...pickByDifficulty(leftover,count-picked.length,diffWeights))}
 }else{
  picked=pickByDifficulty(available,count,diffWeights);
 }
 picked=picked.slice(0,count);
 picked.forEach(q=>used.add(q.id));
 return randomizeSet(picked);
}
/* Fifty-ninth pass: satAdaptive (Full Adaptive SAT / 98-question simulation)
 * and v9Adaptive (numbered Practice Test buttons) are two separate live
 * controllers driving the same SAT adaptive Module-1->Module-2 routing logic,
 * and they had drifted to different thresholds (70% vs 60%) - a student could
 * get routed to the harder Module 2 from one entry point but not the other at
 * the exact same accuracy. Unified to one shared constant so both controllers
 * always agree. 70 matches the official digital SAT's own Module 1 -> Module 2
 * routing behavior more closely than 60 does. */
const SAT_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD=70;
function satAdaptiveStageConfig(stage){return [{section:'Reading & Writing',name:'R&W Module 1',count:27,duration:32*60,route:'mixed'},{section:'Reading & Writing',name:'R&W Module 2',count:27,duration:32*60,route:satAdaptive?.rwRoute||'mixed'},{section:'Math',name:'Math Module 1',count:22,duration:35*60,route:'mixed'},{section:'Math',name:'Math Module 2',count:22,duration:35*60,route:satAdaptive?.mathRoute||'mixed'}][stage]}

function mergeAdaptiveModules(modules){const set=[],answers={},flags=[];modules.forEach(m=>{set.push(...m.set);Object.assign(answers,m.answers);flags.push(...m.flags)});return {set,answers,flags}}

 satAdaptive.active=false;const all=satAdaptive.results,tc=all.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.correct,0),tt=all.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.total,0),ta=all.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.elapsed,0);$v3('satResults').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin',`<div class="overallSummary" id="satAdaptiveOverall"><h3>98-Question Adaptive Simulation Summary</h3><div class="overallGrid"><div><span>Correct</span><b>${tc}/${tt}</b></div><div><span>Practice accuracy</span><b>${pct(tc,tt)}%</b></div><div><span>R&W route</span><b>${satAdaptive.rwRoute==='hard'?'Higher':'Foundational'}</b></div><div><span>Math route</span><b>${satAdaptive.mathRoute==='hard'?'Higher':'Foundational'}</b></div></div><p style="font-size:11px;color:#64748b;margin:10px 0 0">Practice performance only.  actFull.active=false;const all=actFull.results,tc=all.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.correct,0),tt=all.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.total,0);$v3('actResults').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin',`<div class="overallSummary" id="actFullOverall"><h3>131-Question ACT Core Simulation Summary</h3><div class="overallGrid"><div><span>Correct</span><b>${tc}/${tt}</b></div><div><span>Practice accuracy</span><b>${pct(tc,tt)}%</b></div><div><span>English</span><b>${all[0].accuracy}%</b></div><div><span>Math / Reading</span><b>${all[1].accuracy}% / ${all[2].accuracy}%</b></div></div><p style="font-size:11px;color:#64748b;margin:10px 0 0">Practice accuracy is not an official ACT scale score. /* Fifty-ninth pass: choices[1] used to be a hardcoded `part+10` while its
 * rationale claimed it was "the number who did not complete it" (the true
 * complement, total-part) — an external audit caught exactly this
 * mismatch with a worked example (90 members, 30% complete = 27; the old
 * choices[1]=37 was labeled "did not complete" but the real complement is
 * 63). Fixed to actually compute that complement. Also switched the
 * percent cycle from `20+(i%4)*10` (20/30/40/50) to `20+(i%3)*10`
 * (20/30/40 only) — at exactly 50%, part and its complement (total-part)
 * are numerically identical, which would silently create a duplicate
 * answer choice; dropping 50% from the cycle avoids that for every i. */

 * Most existing ACT-ENR-* English items above are template-generated with
 * abstract, category-label choices (e.g. "Create a comma splice" as an answer
 * choice itself, rather than real replacement text) — not the actual format
 * of the real ACT English test, where each item underlines a specific word,
 * phrase, or sentence within a running passage and the choices are literal
 * text alternatives (often including "NO CHANGE"). This site renders each
 * question's `passage` field as plain text (no bold/underline markup), so
 * true visual underlining isn't possible here; instead, each question below
 * quotes the exact tested phrase directly in its own wording, and every
 * choice is real, literal replacement text — the same thing a student would
 * actually have to evaluate on the real test, just identified by quotation

 * checked (each grammar/punctuation rule below was verified against standard
 * usage before being marked correct), covering all three real ACT English
 * reporting domains: Conventions of Standard English, Knowledge of Language,
 * and Production of Writing. */

// ---------- V34: TSIA2 Math coverage expansion — exponential growth/decay, counting &
// combinations, budget/percent-of-total interpretation, sphere volume, cube surface-area-from-
// volume, real-world function evaluation, and target-average problems. These skill types were
// checked against a standard TSI Math prep reference and were not yet represented in the bank.
// All numeric answers are computed programmatically at load time (never hand-typed), and a
// safety-net pass (identical to the one already used for the V20 TSI math batch) removes any
// accidental duplicate choice within a single question. ----------
const V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH=[];

// A. Exponential growth (doubling)
for(let i=1;i<=15;i++){
  const P0=80+20*i, d=2+(i%3), k=1+(i%4), t=d*k;
  const val=P0*Math.pow(2,k);
  const under=P0*Math.pow(2,Math.max(0,k-1));
  const over=P0*Math.pow(2,k+1);
  let linear=P0*(k+1);
  if(linear===val) linear=P0*(k+2); // k=1 degenerate case: P0*(k+1) coincides with P0*2^k
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-EXPG-${i}`,'Mathematics','Quantitative Reasoning — Exponential Growth',i%3===0?'Hard':'Medium',
    `A population of ${P0} bacteria doubles every ${d} hours. About how many bacteria will there be after ${t} hours?`,
    [String(val), String(under), String(over), String(linear)], 0,
    `The population doubles ${k} time(s) in ${t} hours, so the amount is ${P0}×2^${k}=${val}.`,
    ['Correct — multiplies by 2 for each full doubling period.',
     'Uses one fewer doubling period than the time given allows.',
     'Uses one extra doubling period beyond the time given.',
     'Treats the growth as adding a fixed amount each period instead of doubling.'],
    'Divide the elapsed time by the doubling period to find how many times the amount doubles, then multiply by 2 that many times.'));
}

// A2. Exponential decay (half-life)
for(let i=1;i<=10;i++){
  const base=5+i, h=2+(i%3), k=1+(i%4);
  const P0=base*Math.pow(2,4);
  const val=P0/Math.pow(2,k);
  const under=P0/Math.pow(2,Math.max(0,k-1));
  const over=P0/Math.pow(2,k+1);
  const t=h*k;
  let leftoverTrap=P0-val;
  if(leftoverTrap===val) leftoverTrap=P0-val+base; // k=1 degenerate case: P0-val coincides with val when val=P0/2
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-EXPD-${i}`,'Mathematics','Quantitative Reasoning — Exponential Growth','Hard',
    `A sample of ${P0} mg of a substance has a half-life of ${h} hours. About how many milligrams remain after ${t} hours?`,
    [String(val), String(under), String(over), String(leftoverTrap)], 0,
    `In ${t} hours, ${k} half-life period(s) pass, so the remaining amount is ${P0}÷2^${k}=${val} mg.`,
    ['Correct — divides by 2 for each full half-life.',
     'Uses one fewer half-life than the time given allows.',
     'Uses one extra half-life beyond the time given.',
     'Subtracts the remaining amount from the original instead of reporting what is left.'],
    'Divide the elapsed time by the half-life to find how many halvings occur, then divide by 2 that many times.'));
}

// B. Budget / percent-of-total interpretation
const V34_CATS=[['rent','food','transportation','entertainment'],['housing','utilities','groceries','savings'],['tuition','books','housing','personal expenses'],['salaries','equipment','marketing','operations']];
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const total=40000+2000*i;
  const cats=V34_CATS[i%V34_CATS.length];
  const p0=20+(i%10), p1=15+((i+3)%10), p2=10+((i+5)%8);
  const p3=100-p0-p1-p2;
  const pct=[p0,p1,p2,p3];
  const targetIdx=i%4;
  const amt=Math.round(total*pct[targetIdx]/100);
  const wrong1=Math.round(total*pct[(targetIdx+1)%4]/100);
  const wrong2=Math.round(total*(pct[targetIdx]+5)/100);
  const wrong3=Math.round(total/4);
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-BUDG-${i}`,'Mathematics','Quantitative Reasoning — Data Interpretation','Medium',
    `A family's annual income of $${total.toLocaleString()} is divided as follows: ${pct[0]}% ${cats[0]}, ${pct[1]}% ${cats[1]}, ${pct[2]}% ${cats[2]}, and ${pct[3]}% ${cats[3]}. About how much is spent on ${cats[targetIdx]} per year?`,
    [`$${amt.toLocaleString()}`, `$${wrong1.toLocaleString()}`, `$${wrong2.toLocaleString()}`, `$${wrong3.toLocaleString()}`], 0,
    `${pct[targetIdx]}% of $${total.toLocaleString()} is ${(pct[targetIdx]/100)}×$${total.toLocaleString()}=$${amt.toLocaleString()}.`,
    ['Correct percent of the total.',
     "This is the amount for a different category in the breakdown, not the one asked about.",
     'Uses an incorrect percentage that does not match the stated breakdown.',
     'Divides the total evenly into four equal parts, ignoring the actual percentages given.'],
    'Convert the percent to a decimal and multiply by the total amount.'));
}

// C. Combinations / counting
function v34Factorial(x){let r=1;for(let j=2;j<=x;j++)r*=j;return r;}
function v34nCr(N,K){return Math.round(v34Factorial(N)/(v34Factorial(K)*v34Factorial(N-K)));}
function v34nPr(N,K){return Math.round(v34Factorial(N)/v34Factorial(N-K));}
let v34CombI=0;
for(let nn=5;nn<=10;nn++){
 for(let kk=2;kk<=4;kk++){
  const n=nn, k=kk;
  const correct=v34nCr(n,k);
  const permTrap=v34nPr(n,k);
  const multTrap=n*k;
  // Skip the one (n,k) pair in this range where n*k coincidentally equals C(n,k)
  // (n=5,k=2: both are 10) — a "multiplication trap" distractor is meaningless if it
  // can't actually be distinguished from the correct answer for that pair.
  if(multTrap===correct) continue;
  v34CombI++;
  const i=v34CombI;
  const nearMiss=correct+n;
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-COMB-${i}`,'Mathematics','Probabilistic and Statistical Reasoning — Counting Principles','Hard',
    `A student must choose ${k} books to bring on a trip from a shelf of ${n} different books. How many different groups of ${k} books are possible?`,
    [String(correct), String(permTrap), String(multTrap), String(nearMiss)], 0,
    `Since the order the books are chosen does not matter, use combinations: C(${n},${k})=${n}!/(${k}!×${n-k}!)=${correct}.`,
    ['Correct — uses combinations because order does not matter.',
     'This is the number of permutations, which incorrectly treats different orders as different groups.',
     'Multiplies the two numbers directly instead of applying the combination formula.',
     'An arithmetic slip while applying the combination formula.'],
    'When the order of selection does not matter, use the combination formula C(n,k)=n!/(k!(n−k)!).'));
 }
}

// D. Sphere volume
for(let i=1;i<=15;i++){
  const r=3*i;
  const coeff=Math.round((4/3)*Math.pow(r,3));
  const noFactor=Math.pow(r,3);
  let surfaceConfusion=4*Math.pow(r,2);
  if(surfaceConfusion===coeff) surfaceConfusion=4*Math.pow(r,2)+r; // r=3 degenerate case: (4/3)r^3 coincides with 4r^2
  const coneConfusion=Math.round((1/3)*Math.pow(r,3));
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-SPHV-${i}`,'Mathematics','Geometric and Spatial Reasoning — Volume','Medium',
    `A sphere has a radius of ${r} units. What is its volume, in terms of π?`,
    [`${coeff}π`, `${noFactor}π`, `${surfaceConfusion}π`, `${coneConfusion}π`], 0,
    `Volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(${r})³ = ${coeff}π.`,
    ['Correct sphere volume formula.',
     'Leaves out the 4/3 factor from the volume formula.',
     'Uses the surface area formula (4πr²) instead of the volume formula.',
     'Uses the cone volume formula ((1/3)πr³) instead of the sphere volume formula.'],
    'Use V=(4/3)πr³ for the volume of a sphere.'));
}

// E. Cube: surface area from volume
for(let i=1;i<=15;i++){
  const s=1+i;
  const vol=Math.pow(s,3);
  const correctSA=6*Math.pow(s,2);
  const forgot6=Math.pow(s,2);
  const usedS=6*s;
  let volChoice=vol;
  if(volChoice===correctSA) volChoice=vol+s; // s=6 degenerate case: volume coincides with surface area
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-CUBESA-${i}`,'Mathematics','Geometric and Spatial Reasoning — Area','Medium',
    `A cube has a volume of ${vol} cubic centimeters. What is its total surface area, in square centimeters?`,
    [String(correctSA), String(forgot6), String(usedS), String(volChoice)], 0,
    `The edge length is the cube root of ${vol}, which is ${s}. Surface area = 6×(edge)² = 6×${s}²=${correctSA}.`,
    ['Correct — finds the edge length, then applies the surface area formula for a cube.',
     'Finds the edge length but forgets to multiply by the 6 faces.',
     'Multiplies the edge length by 6 without squaring it first.',
     'Repeats the given volume instead of computing surface area.'],
    'Find the edge length by taking the cube root of the volume, then use surface area = 6×(edge length)².'));
}

// F. Real-world function evaluation
for(let i=1;i<=20;i++){
  const C=20+5*(i%6), r=11+2*(i%7), m=2+(i%10);
  const val=r*m+C;
  const forgotFlat=r*m;
  const addedInstead=r+m+C;
  const swapped=C*m+r;
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-FNREAL-${i}`,'Mathematics','Algebraic Reasoning — Functions','Medium',
    `A cable company charges a $${C} equipment fee plus $${r} per month of service. The total cost after m months is given by f(m) = ${r}m + ${C}. What is f(${m}), the total cost after ${m} months?`,
    [`$${val}`, `$${forgotFlat}`, `$${addedInstead}`, `$${swapped}`], 0,
    `Substitute m=${m}: f(${m}) = ${r}(${m}) + ${C} = ${r*m} + ${C} = $${val}.`,
    ['Correct substitution and evaluation.',
     'Leaves out the flat equipment fee.',
     'Adds the rate and the number of months instead of multiplying them.',
     'Switches the roles of the flat fee and the monthly rate.'],
    'Substitute the given value for m into the function, then apply order of operations (multiply before adding).'));
}

// G. Target average ("how many more points needed")
for(let i=1;i<=20;i++){
  const n=4+(i%3);
  const existing=[]; let sum=0;
  for(let j=0;j<n-1;j++){ const s=72+((i*7+j*13)%20); existing.push(s); sum+=s; }
  const desiredNeeded=82+(i%13);
  let target=Math.round((sum+desiredNeeded)/n);
  let needed=target*n-sum;
  const avgExisting=Math.round(sum/(n-1));
  if(needed===target){ target=target+1; needed=target*n-sum; } // degenerate case: target average happened to equal the existing average, collapsing needed/target/avgExisting to one number
  const offByCount=target*(n-2>=1?n-2:1)-sum;
  V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.push(O(`TSIA2-V34-M-AVGT-${i}`,'Mathematics','Probabilistic and Statistical Reasoning — Mean','Hard',
    `A student's first ${n-1} test scores are ${existing.join(', ')}. What score does the student need on the ${n===4?'4th':n===5?'5th':'6th'} test to have an average of exactly ${target} across all ${n} tests?`,
    [String(needed), String(target), String(avgExisting), String(offByCount)], 0,
    `To average ${target} over ${n} tests, the total must be ${target}×${n}=${target*n}. The first ${n-1} tests already total ${sum}, so the needed score is ${target*n}−${sum}=${needed}.`,
    ['Correct — solves for the missing score using the total needed for the target average.',
     'This is the target average itself, not the score needed to reach it.',
     'This is the average of the scores already recorded, not the score still needed.',
     'Uses the wrong number of tests when finding the required total.'],
    'Multiply the target average by the total number of tests to find the required total, then subtract the sum of the known scores.'));
}

// Safety net: nudge any accidental duplicate numeric distractor (never touches index 0, the correct answer)
V34_ENRICHMENT_TSIA2_MATH.forEach(q=>{
  const seen=new Set([q.choices[0]]);
  for(let i=1;i<4;i++){
    let val=q.choices[i];
    while(seen.has(val)){
      const n=parseFloat(val);
      val=(!isNaN(n) && String(n)===val)?String(n+1):val+'*';
    }
    q.choices[i]=val;seen.add(val);
  }
});

// ================= V36 SAT ENRICHMENT (Math Geometry & Trig + Reading/Writing) =================
const V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO=[];

// Helpers
function v36gcd(a,b){a=Math.abs(a);b=Math.abs(b);while(b){[a,b]=[b,a%b]}return a}
function v36frac(num,den){const g=v36gcd(num,den)||1;let n=num/g,d=den/g;if(d<0){n=-n;d=-d}return [n,d]}
function v36shuffleSafe(choices,correctIdx){
  // site's established safety-net duplicate nudge, reused verbatim in spirit
  const seen=new Set([String(choices[0]).trim().toLowerCase()]);
  for(let i=1;i<choices.length;i++){
    let key=String(choices[i]).trim().toLowerCase();
    while(seen.has(key)){
      const num=Number(choices[i]);
      if(!isNaN(num)&&String(choices[i])===String(num)){choices[i]=String(num+1)}
      else{choices[i]=choices[i]+"*"}
      key=String(choices[i]).trim().toLowerCase();
    }
    seen.add(key);
  }
  return choices;
}

// ===================== A. Circle equations (translation) — 25 =====================
// (x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2, circle A given, shift by (dx,dy) to get circle B; find equation of circle B.
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const h=(i%7)-3;           // -3..3
  const k=((i*3)%9)-4;       // -4..4
  const r=3+(i%6);           // 3..8
  const dx=1+(i%4);          // shift right by dx (or left if i odd flips sign)
  const dy=1+((i+2)%4);
  const dirX=(i%2===0)?1:-1;
  const dirY=(i%3===0)?1:-1;
  const newH=h+dirX*dx;
  const newK=k+dirY*dy;
  const r2=r*r;
  function fmtCircle(hh,kk,rr2){
    const xTerm = hh===0? "x^2" : `(x ${hh>0?'-':'+'} ${Math.abs(hh)})^2`;
    const yTerm = kk===0? "y^2" : `(y ${kk>0?'-':'+'} ${Math.abs(kk)})^2`;
    return `${xTerm} + ${yTerm} = ${rr2}`;
  }
  const origEq = fmtCircle(h,k,r2);
  const correctEq = fmtCircle(newH,newK,r2);
  const distractor1 = fmtCircle(h+dirX*dx, k, r2); // only shifted x
  const distractor2 = fmtCircle(h, k+dirY*dy, r2); // only shifted y
  const distractor3 = fmtCircle(h-dirX*dx, k-dirY*dy, r2); // shifted wrong direction
  const dirWord = (dirX>0?"right":"left")+" "+dx+" units and "+(dirY>0?"up":"down")+" "+dy+" units";
  let choices=[correctEq, distractor1, distractor2, distractor3];
  choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
  const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(correctEq);
  V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
    id:`SAT-V36-GEO-CIRC-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
    q:`The equation ${origEq} represents circle A in the xy-plane. Circle B is obtained by translating circle A ${dirWord}. Which of the following equations represents circle B?`,
    choices, a: correctIdx,
    ex:`Translating a circle only changes the center (h, k), not the radius. Circle A has center (${h}, ${k}) and radius ${r}. Shifting ${dirWord} moves the center to (${newH}, ${newK}), giving ${correctEq}.`,
    why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: applies both the horizontal and vertical shift to the center while keeping r^2 = ${r2}.` : `Incorrect: does not apply both shifts correctly to the center coordinates.`),
    strategy:"A translation changes only the circle's center (h, k); the radius (and r^2 on the right side) never changes."
  });
}

// ===================== B. Right triangle trig cofunction identity — 25 =====================
// Triangle JKL, angle J = 90 degrees, so K and L are complementary: sin(L) = cos(K), cos(L) = sin(K).
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const denom = 25 + (i%12)*4; // varied denominators 25..69
  let num = 5 + (i%(denom-6)); // numerator less than denom, avoid 0
  if(num>=denom) num = denom-7;
  const [n,d]=v36frac(num,denom);
  const askSin = i%2===0;
  const givenFn = askSin ? "cos" : "sin";
  const askFn = askSin ? "sin" : "cos";
  const correct = `${n}/${d}`;
  // distractors: same fraction flipped, denom-num over denom, and a shifted-by-2 numerator (all as reduced-looking fractions, kept as literal strings so they read naturally)
  const flip = `${d}/${n}`;
  const complementWrong = `${d-n}/${d}`;
  const shifted = `${Math.max(1,n-2)}/${d}`;
  let choices=[correct, flip, complementWrong, shifted];
  choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
  const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(correct);
  V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
    id:`SAT-V36-GEO-TRIG-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
    q:`In triangle JKL, angle J is a right angle, and ${givenFn}(K) = ${n}/${d}. What is the value of ${askFn}(L)?`,
    choices, a: correctIdx,
    ex:`Since angle J is a right angle, angles K and L are complementary (they sum to 90°). For complementary angles, sin of one equals cos of the other: sin(L) = cos(K) and cos(L) = sin(K). Since ${givenFn}(K) = ${n}/${d}, it follows that ${askFn}(L) = ${n}/${d}.`,
    why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: uses the cofunction identity for complementary angles K and L.` : `Incorrect: does not correctly apply the sin/cos cofunction relationship for complementary angles.`),
    strategy:"When one angle of a right triangle is 90°, the other two angles are complementary, so sin of one equals cos of the other."
  });
}

// ===================== C. 3D volume & surface area — 25 =====================
const V36_SOLIDS = ['rectangular prism','cylinder','cone','sphere'];
const v36KindCounts = {};
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const kind = V36_SOLIDS[i%4];
  const n = (v36KindCounts[kind] = (v36KindCounts[kind]||0) + 1); // per-kind counter, decoupled from outer i%4 selector
  let q,ex,correct,d1,d2,d3,skillNote;
  if(kind==='rectangular prism'){
    const l=2+(n%6), w=3+(n%5), h=4+(n%7);
    correct = l*w*h;
    d1 = 2*(l*w+w*h+l*h); // surface area confused for volume
    d2 = l*w; d3 = l+w+h;
    q = `A rectangular prism has length ${l} cm, width ${w} cm, and height ${h} cm. What is the volume of the prism, in cubic centimeters?`;
    ex = `Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height = ${l} × ${w} × ${h} = ${correct}.`;
  } else if(kind==='cylinder'){
    const r=2+(n%5), h=3+(n%6);
    correct = `${r*r*h}π`;
    d1 = `${2*r*h}π`; d2 = `${r*h}π`; d3 = `${2*r*r*h}π`;
    q = `A cylinder has a radius of ${r} cm and a height of ${h} cm. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cubic centimeters, in terms of π?`;
    ex = `Volume of a cylinder = π r^2 h = π(${r})^2(${h}) = ${r*r*h}π.`;
  } else if(kind==='cone'){
    const r=3+(n%7), h=3+(n%6);
    const base = r*r*h;
    const g = v36gcd(base,3);
    correct = g===3 ? `${base/3}π` : `${base}π/3`;
    d1 = `${base}π`; d2 = `${(r*h)}π/3`; d3 = `${base*3}π`;
    q = `A cone has a radius of ${r} cm and a height of ${h} cm. What is the volume of the cone, in cubic centimeters, in terms of π?`;
    ex = `Volume of a cone = (1/3)π r^2 h = (1/3)π(${r})^2(${h}) = ${correct}.`;
  } else {
    const r=2+(n%9);
    const base = 4*r*r*r;
    const g = v36gcd(base,3);
    correct = g===3 ? `${base/3}π` : `${base}π/3`;
    d1 = `${4*r*r}π`; d2 = `${base}π`; d3 = `${base*3}π`;
    q = `A sphere has a radius of ${r} cm. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic centimeters, in terms of π?`;
    ex = `Volume of a sphere = (4/3)π r^3 = (4/3)π(${r})^3 = ${correct}.`;
  }
  let choices=[String(correct), String(d1), String(d2), String(d3)];
  choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
  const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(String(correct));
  V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
    id:`SAT-V36-GEO-VOL-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
    q, choices, a: correctIdx===-1?0:correctIdx,
    ex,
    why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===(correctIdx===-1?0:correctIdx) ? `Correct: applies the correct volume formula for a ${kind}.` : `Incorrect: uses the wrong formula or a formula for a different measurement (such as surface area) instead of volume.`),
    strategy:"Match the shape to its volume formula before substituting: prism = lwh, cylinder = πr^2h, cone = (1/3)πr^2h, sphere = (4/3)πr^3."
  });
}

// ===================== D. Arc length & sector area — 25 =====================
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const r = 4+(i%9); // 4..12
  const angles = [30,45,60,90,120,135,150,180,240,270];
  const theta = angles[i%angles.length];
  const askArc = i%2===0;
  const frac = theta/360;
  function fracStr(numDeg){
    const [n,d]=v36frac(numDeg,360);
    return [n,d];
  }
  const [fn,fd]=fracStr(theta);
  let correct, d1, d2, d3, q, ex;
  if(askArc){
    // arc length = (theta/360) * 2*pi*r = (fn/fd)*2r * pi
    const coeffNum = fn*2*r, coeffDen = fd;
    const [cn,cd]=v36frac(coeffNum,coeffDen);
    correct = cd===1 ? `${cn}π` : `${cn}π/${cd}`;
    d1 = cd===1 ? `${cn*2}π` : `${cn*2}π/${cd}`; // forgot factor of 2 (used r instead of 2r... actually doubled)
    d2 = `${r}π`; // ignored angle fraction entirely
    const [dn,dd]=v36frac(fn*r,fd);
    d3 = dd===1? `${dn}π` : `${dn}π/${dd}`; // used r instead of 2r (radius instead of diameter factor)
    q = `A circle has a radius of ${r} units. What is the length of an arc on the circle formed by a central angle of ${theta} degrees, in terms of π?`;
    ex = `Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr = (${theta}/360) × 2π(${r}) = ${correct}.`;
  } else {
    // sector area = (theta/360) * pi*r^2
    const coeffNum = fn*r*r, coeffDen=fd;
    const [cn,cd]=v36frac(coeffNum,coeffDen);
    correct = cd===1 ? `${cn}π` : `${cn}π/${cd}`;
    d1 = cd===1 ? `${cn*2}π` : `${cn*2}π/${cd}`;
    d2 = `${r*r}π`;
    const [dn,dd]=v36frac(fn*r,fd);
    d3 = dd===1? `${dn}π` : `${dn}π/${dd}`;
    q = `A circle has a radius of ${r} units. What is the area of a sector of the circle formed by a central angle of ${theta} degrees, in terms of π?`;
    ex = `Sector area = (θ/360) × πr^2 = (${theta}/360) × π(${r})^2 = ${correct}.`;
  }
  let choices=[correct, d1, d2, d3];
  choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
  const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(correct);
  V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
    id:`SAT-V36-GEO-ARC-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
    q, choices, a: correctIdx,
    ex,
    why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: multiplies the full-circle formula by the correct central-angle fraction θ/360.` : `Incorrect: misapplies the angle fraction or the radius in the formula.`),
    strategy:"Both arc length and sector area start from the full-circle formula (2πr or πr^2) multiplied by θ/360."
  });
}

// ===================== E. Parallel lines & transversal (described in words) — 25 =====================
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const A=2+(i%5), B=3+(i%9), C=3+(i%4), D=1+(i%11);
  const k = i+3; // choose k directly to guarantee clean integers, then derive expressions to match
  const xVal = A*k+B;
  const yVal = 180 - xVal; // co-interior angles are supplementary by construction
  // Build the C,D expression to equal yVal exactly: C*k + D = yVal  => D = yVal - C*k
  const Dfix = yVal - C*k;
  const zVal = yVal; // z is corresponding to the (C k + Dfix) angle, so equal to it
  let choices=[String(zVal), String(xVal), String(180-zVal), String(zVal+ (i%5)+2)];
  choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
  const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(String(zVal));
  V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
    id:`SAT-V36-GEO-PAR-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
    q:`Lines m and n are parallel and are both crossed by transversal t. At line m, one of the interior angles measures (${A}k + ${B})° . At line n, the interior angle on the same side of the transversal measures (${C}k ${Dfix>=0?'+':'-'} ${Math.abs(Dfix)})°, and this angle is supplementary to the angle at line m. Angle z is formed at line n and corresponds to the (${C}k ${Dfix>=0?'+':'-'} ${Math.abs(Dfix)})° angle. What is the value of z?`,
    choices, a: correctIdx,
    ex:`Same-side interior angles formed by a transversal crossing parallel lines are supplementary, so (${A}k + ${B}) + (${C}k ${Dfix>=0?'+':'-'} ${Math.abs(Dfix)}) = 180. Solving gives k = ${k}, so the angle at line n measures ${yVal}°. Since z corresponds to that angle and corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, z = ${zVal}.`,
    why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: solves for k using the supplementary relationship, then uses the corresponding-angles rule.` : `Incorrect: misapplies the supplementary or corresponding angle relationship.`),
    strategy:"With parallel lines cut by a transversal: same-side interior angles are supplementary (sum to 180°); corresponding angles are equal."
  });
}

// ===================== F. Pythagorean theorem / distance formula — 25 =====================
const V36_BASE_TRIPLES=[[3,4,5],[5,12,13],[8,15,17],[7,24,25],[20,21,29],[9,40,41],[11,60,61],[12,35,37],[13,84,85],[16,63,65]];
// Pre-build a de-duplicated pool of scaled triples (by actual (leg,leg,hyp) value, not by index) so no two
// different (triple, scale) picks can coincidentally produce the same numeric triangle.
const V36_PYTH_POOL = [];
{
  const seenTriples = new Set();
  outer:
  for(const scale of [1,2,3]){
    for(const [a,b,c] of V36_BASE_TRIPLES){
      const legA=a*scale, legB=b*scale, hyp=c*scale;
      const key = `${legA},${legB},${hyp}`;
      if(seenTriples.has(key)) continue;
      seenTriples.add(key);
      V36_PYTH_POOL.push([legA,legB,hyp]);
      if(V36_PYTH_POOL.length>=13) break outer; // need 13 for the !useDistance branch (i=1,3,...,25)
    }
  }
}
let v36PythIdx=0;
for(let i=1;i<=25;i++){
  const useDistance = i%2===0;
  if(!useDistance){
    const [legA,legB,hyp]=V36_PYTH_POOL[v36PythIdx++];
    const askHyp = (v36PythIdx%3!==0);
    let correct,d1,d2,d3,q;
    if(askHyp){
      correct=hyp; d1=legA+legB; d2=Math.abs(legA-legB); d3=hyp+2;
      q=`A right triangle has legs of length ${legA} and ${legB}. What is the length of the hypotenuse?`;
    } else {
      correct=legB; d1=hyp; d2=legA; d3=legB+2;
      q=`A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length ${hyp} and one leg of length ${legA}. What is the length of the other leg?`;
    }
    let choices=[String(correct), String(d1), String(d2), String(d3)];
    choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
    const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(String(correct));
    V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
      id:`SAT-V36-GEO-PYTH-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
      q, choices, a: correctIdx,
      ex: askHyp ? `By the Pythagorean theorem, c^2 = a^2 + b^2 = ${legA}^2 + ${legB}^2 = ${legA*legA} + ${legB*legB} = ${legA*legA+legB*legB}. Taking the square root gives c = ${hyp}.` : `By the Pythagorean theorem, b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = ${hyp}^2 - ${legA}^2 = ${hyp*hyp} - ${legA*legA} = ${hyp*hyp-legA*legA}. Taking the square root gives b = ${legB}.`,
      why: choices.map((c2,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: correctly applies a^2 + b^2 = c^2.` : `Incorrect: adds or subtracts the wrong pair of sides.`),
      strategy:"In a right triangle, a^2 + b^2 = c^2, where c is always the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle)."
    });
  } else {
    const x1=(i%7)-3, y1=((i*2)%9)-4, dx=2+(i%6), dy=3+((i+1)%5);
    const x2=x1+dx, y2=y1+dy;
    const distSq = dx*dx+dy*dy;
    let sqrtVal=Math.sqrt(distSq);
    let correct, isPerfect = Number.isInteger(sqrtVal);
    correct = isPerfect ? String(sqrtVal) : `√${distSq}`;
    const d1 = isPerfect ? String(sqrtVal+2) : `√${distSq+ (i%4)+1}`;
    const d2 = String(dx+dy);
    const d3 = isPerfect ? String(Math.max(1,sqrtVal-2)) : `√${Math.max(2,distSq-4)}`;
    let choices=[correct, d1, d2, d3];
    choices=v36shuffleSafe(choices,0);
    const correctIdx=choices.indexOf(correct);
    V36_ENRICHMENT_SAT_GEO.push({
      id:`SAT-V36-GEO-DIST-${i}`, exam:"SAT", section:"Math", skill:"Geometry & Trigonometry", difficulty: i<=8?"Easy":i<=18?"Medium":"Hard",
      q:`In the xy-plane, what is the distance between the points (${x1}, ${y1}) and (${x2}, ${y2})?`,
      choices, a: correctIdx,
      ex:`Using the distance formula, d = √[(x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2] = √[(${dx})^2 + (${dy})^2] = √${distSq}${isPerfect?` = ${sqrtVal}`:''}.`,
      why: choices.map((c,idx)=> idx===correctIdx ? `Correct: correctly applies the distance formula to both coordinate differences.` : `Incorrect: uses only one coordinate difference or combines them incorrectly.`),
      strategy:"The distance formula is the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences between two points."
    });
  }
}

/* Fifty-ninth pass: v17BalanceAnswerPositions (defined earlier) was only ever
 * applied to the V17 batch, at the point in the file where that batch was
 * built — every generator added by later passes (V9, V22, V32, etc.) kept
 * whatever correct-answer index its own generator hardcoded, and many of
 * those generators always put the correct choice first (index 0). An audit
 * of the exported bank confirmed a real, measurable skew here (e.g. ACT
 * choice A/D each ~36% of questions vs. an even 25%). Re-running the exact
 * same rotation against the FULLY assembled, deduplicated bank fixes this
 * for every question regardless of which pass generated it, using each
 * question's final served index (idx%4) as the rotation amount — this is
 * safe to layer on top of the earlier partial pass since rotation composes,
 * and it's what makes the SCOREPATH_V17_BANK_REPORT note below ("balanced in
 * the bank") actually true rather than aspirational. */
v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.SAT);v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.ACT);v17BalanceAnswerPositions(PRO_BANK.TSIA2);
window.ScorePathBank=PRO_BANK;
// Exposed so question-bank-core.js's single-section/diagnostic/timed practice
// builders (selectSet/satSet/actSet) can draw from the same full, deduplicated
// bank using the same blueprint-domain-proportional + difficulty-weighted
// sampling the "Practice Test 1-5" adaptive simulations already use, instead
// of the small original arrays those functions used to be limited to.
window.ScorePathAdaptivePick=adaptivePick;

/* ---------- V18: Adaptive-by-module SAT Practice Tests (Module 1 fixed, Module 2 routes on M1 accuracy) ---------- */
let v9Adaptive=null;
/* Real Digital SAT section lengths (54 Reading & Writing across 2 modules of
 * 27, 44 Math across 2 modules of 22 = 98 total; 32 min/R&W module, 35
 * min/Math module) — same numbers satAdaptiveStageConfig above already
 * uses for the single unnumbered "Full Adaptive SAT" button. Before this,
 * each numbered "Practice Test" was only 28 questions (7 per module), a
 * quick abbreviated drill, not a real-length practice test — fixed so a
 * student taking "Practice Test 1" gets the same real, full 98-question
 * experience as "Full Adaptive SAT," just with its own fresh seed. */
function v9AdaptiveStageConfig(stage){return [{section:'Reading & Writing',name:'R&W Module 1',count:27,duration:32*60,route:'mixed'},{section:'Reading & Writing',name:'R&W Module 2',count:27,duration:32*60,route:v9Adaptive?.rwRoute||'mixed'},{section:'Math',name:'Math Module 1',count:22,duration:35*60,route:'mixed'},{section:'Math',name:'Math Module 2',count:22,duration:35*60,route:v9Adaptive?.mathRoute||'mixed'}][stage]}
function v9LaunchAdaptiveStage(){const cfg=v9AdaptiveStageConfig(v9Adaptive.stage),pool=(cfg.section==='Math'?PRO_BANK.SAT.filter(q=>q.section==='Math'):PRO_BANK.SAT.filter(q=>q.section==='Reading & Writing')),set=adaptivePick(pool,cfg.count,cfg.route,v9Adaptive.used,'SAT',cfg.section);if(set.length<cfg.count){alert('This practice test module could not be built with enough unique questions.');v9Adaptive.active=false;return}cacheSet(satStore,set);saveSAT();satHideAll();$v3('satAdaptiveBreak')?.classList.remove('show');$v3('satPracticeShell').classList.add('show');satState={set,i:0,answers:{},confidence:{},flags:[],timed:true,start:Date.now(),seconds:cfg.duration,timerId:null,mode:`v9-sat-pt${v9Adaptive.num}-${v9Adaptive.stage+1}`,submitted:{},duration:cfg.duration,sessionCode:sessionCode('SAT')};$v3('satTestTitle').textContent=`SAT Practice Test ${v9Adaptive.num} — ${cfg.name}`;$v3('satModeLabel').textContent=`Adaptive Timed Practice • Module ${v9Adaptive.stage+1} of 4`;$v3('satConfidenceBox')?.classList.add('hidden');$v3('satSubmitBtn').classList.add('hidden');beginPacing('sat',satState,'satTimer',finishSAT,cfg.duration);renderSAT();location.hash='sat-center'}
const finishSATBeforeV18=finishSAT;
finishSAT=function(auto=false){
 if(v9Adaptive?.active){const cfg=v9AdaptiveStageConfig(v9Adaptive.stage),correct=satState.set.filter(q=>satState.answers[q.id]===q.a).length,total=satState.set.length,accuracy=pct(correct,total),elapsed=Math.max(0,satState.duration-satState.seconds),isFinal=v9Adaptive.stage===3;v9Adaptive.modules.push({set:satState.set,answers:{...satState.answers},flags:[...satState.flags]});cacheSet(satStore,satState.set);const thisModuleState=satState;if(isFinal){const priorModules=v9Adaptive.modules.slice(0,-1);let priorAnswered=0,priorCorrect=0;priorModules.forEach(m=>m.set.forEach(q=>{if(m.answers[q.id]!==undefined){priorAnswered++;if(m.answers[q.id]===q.a)priorCorrect++}}));satStore.answered-=priorAnswered;satStore.correct-=priorCorrect;const merged=mergeAdaptiveModules(v9Adaptive.modules),totalElapsed=v9Adaptive.results.reduce((n,x)=>n+x.elapsed,0)+elapsed;satState={...thisModuleState,set:merged.set,answers:merged.answers,flags:merged.flags,duration:totalElapsed,seconds:0,mode:`v9-sat-pt${v9Adaptive.num}-full`};cacheSet(satStore,satState.set)}finishSATBeforeV18(auto);if(!isFinal)satState=thisModuleState;v9Adaptive.results.push({name:cfg.name,section:cfg.section,correct,total,accuracy,elapsed,route:cfg.route});if(v9Adaptive.stage===0)v9Adaptive.rwRoute=accuracy>=SAT_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD?'hard':'foundation';if(v9Adaptive.stage===2)v9Adaptive.mathRoute=accuracy>=SAT_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD?'hard':'foundation';if(v9Adaptive.stage<3){v9Adaptive.stage++;$v3('satResults').classList.remove('show');$v3('satAdaptiveBreak').classList.add('show');const next=v9AdaptiveStageConfig(v9Adaptive.stage);$v3('satAdaptiveBreakTitle').textContent=`${cfg.name} complete`;$v3('satAdaptiveBreakText').innerHTML=`You answered <b>${correct} of ${total}</b> correctly (${accuracy}%). ${cfg.section==='Reading & Writing'&&v9Adaptive.stage===1?`Your Reading & Writing Module 2 will use the <span class="routePill">${routeLabel(accuracy)}</span>.`:cfg.section==='Math'&&v9Adaptive.stage===3?`Your Math Module 2 will use the <span class="routePill">${routeLabel(accuracy)}</span>.`:`Next: <b>${next.name}</b>.`}`;$v3('satAdaptiveBreakStats').innerHTML=`<div class="moduleBreakStat"><span>Accuracy</span><b>${accuracy}%</b></div><div class="moduleBreakStat"><span>Correct</span><b>${correct}/${total}</b></div><div class="moduleBreakStat"><span>Next</span><b>${next.name}</b></div>`;location.hash='sat-center';renderStudentHub();return}v9Adaptive.active=false;const This is not an official SAT score conversion. Module 2 difficulty was adjusted based on your Module 1 accuracy, mirroring how the real Digital SAT adapts. The full review and mistake list below cover all ${tt} questions across every module.</p></div>`);renderStudentHub();return}
 finishSATBeforeV18(auto)
};

/* ---------- V19: ACT Practice Tests (real 131-question length; the real ACT is a fixed, non-adaptive test, so — unlike SAT/TSIA2 above — there's no module-2-routes-on-module-1 branching here, just the real exam's own 3 sections) ---------- */

/* ---------- V22: Rich post-test question review ----------
 * Replaces the generic "doğru/yanlış + explanation" review card with a
 * guided per-question breakdown: Result → Your Answer → Correct Answer →
 * Why You Missed It → Step-by-Step → Verification → Choice Analysis →
 * Strategy → Skill/Difficulty/Time → Mistake Type → Similar Question →
 * Mastery → Next Question — the exact order requested, built on top of
 * the why[] data-quality fix above (every wrong choice now has its own
 * distinct explanation instead of one generic phrase repeated 3×). */

// -- second, larger why[]-quality fix: the SAT-ENR/ACT-ENR/TSIA2-ENR
// families (2,121 questions — the single biggest chunk of the bank) were
// built from one shared template: every wrong choice's rationale reads
// `"<choice text>" does not match: <the correct answer's own justification,
// repeated verbatim>` — so it LOOKS distinct per choice (the quoted choice
// text differs) but the actual REASON is identical for all three wrong
// answers, which is exactly the generic-explanation problem flagged for
// this project. This rewrites each wrong choice's rationale to explain why
// THAT specific choice fails, using the choice's own wording, instead of
// restating the correct answer's justification three times over.
/* v58: these three fallback strings are the ones v22FixTemplatedWhy reaches
 * for whenever v22CategorizeWrongReason can't match a keyword (or the
 * question already used that category for an earlier wrong choice) — which
 * turned out to happen for roughly 900 of TSIA2's 1,568 questions (57%),
 * mostly plain math computations and single-word grammar blanks. The
 * original three fallbacks were written in reading-comprehension language
 * ("the passage", "the given evidence", "the main point being tested"),
 * which is meaningless attached to e.g. a percent calculation or a
 * punctuation blank with no passage at all (a zero-error-audit finding, not
 * previously caught). Rewritten to be true regardless of question type. */
const V22_FALLBACK_REASONS=[
  c=>`"${c}" does not correctly complete or answer what this specific question asks.`,
  c=>`"${c}" fails to satisfy the rule, calculation, or requirement the question is testing.`,
  c=>`"${c}" looks plausible at a glance, but does not hold up when checked against the question's actual requirement.`
];
function v22CategorizeWrongReason(choiceText){
  const c=choiceText;
  if(/comma splice|run-on|fragment|dangling|misplaced|redundant|wordy|awkward|ambiguous|passive voice|subject-verb|agreement/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" introduces its own grammar or clarity problem rather than fixing the original one.`,'grammar'];
  if(/remove|delete|omit/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" strips out something the sentence or passage actually needs.`,'remove'];
  if(/universal|every ?[a-z]*|all |always|no matter|entire|everyone|everything|forever/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" overgeneralizes far beyond what the passage's evidence actually supports.`,'overgeneral'];
  if(/no |not |never|zero|nothing|cancel|closed|refused|denies|contradict|opposite|decreased|dropped|failed|no such/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" contradicts what the passage or question actually states.`,'contradict'];
  if(/unrelated|irrelevant|different topic|another subject|nothing to do with/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" addresses something outside what the passage or question is actually about.`,'unrelated'];
  if(/definition|procedure|instructions|steps|technical manual/i.test(c))
    return [`"${c}" answers a different kind of question than the one actually being asked.`,'wrongtype'];
  return [null,null];
}
function v22FixTemplatedWhy(bank){
  if(!Array.isArray(bank))return;
  const re=/^"(.*)" does not match: /;
  bank.forEach(q=>{
    if(!q||!Array.isArray(q.why)||q.why.length!==4)return;
    let wrongSlot=0;const usedCategories=new Set();
    q.why=q.why.map((w,i)=>{
      if(i===q.a)return w;
      const m=typeof w==='string'&&w.match(re);
      if(!m){wrongSlot++;return w}
      const choiceText=m[1];
      let [text,cat]=v22CategorizeWrongReason(choiceText);
      // If this question already used that category for an earlier wrong
      // choice (or no keyword matched at all), fall back to a positional
      // reason instead — guarantees every wrong choice reads differently,
      // never repeating the same rationale twice in one question.
      if(!text||usedCategories.has(cat)){text=V22_FALLBACK_REASONS[wrongSlot%V22_FALLBACK_REASONS.length](choiceText);cat='fallback'+wrongSlot}
      usedCategories.add(cat);wrongSlot++;
      return text;
    });
  });
}
v22FixTemplatedWhy(PRO_BANK.SAT);v22FixTemplatedWhy(PRO_BANK.ACT);v22FixTemplatedWhy(PRO_BANK.TSIA2);

// -- per-question elapsed time, captured live during the test so the
// review can show "Your Time" against a per-section pacing target. --
const v22Timing={},v22Active={};
function v22Enter(examKey,q){
  if(!q)return;const now=Date.now(),cur=v22Active[examKey];
  if(cur&&cur.id&&cur.id!==q.id){v22Timing[examKey]=v22Timing[examKey]||{};v22Timing[examKey][cur.id]=(v22Timing[examKey][cur.id]||0)+(now-cur.enteredAt)/1000}
  if(!cur||cur.id!==q.id)v22Active[examKey]={id:q.id,enteredAt:now};
}
function v22Flush(examKey){
  const cur=v22Active[examKey];
  if(cur&&cur.id){v22Timing[examKey]=v22Timing[examKey]||{};v22Timing[examKey][cur.id]=(v22Timing[examKey][cur.id]||0)+(Date.now()-cur.enteredAt)/1000;v22Active[examKey]=null}
}
function v22TimeFor(examKey,id){const t=v22Timing[examKey]&&v22Timing[examKey][id];return t===undefined?null:Math.round(t)}
const v22PrevRenderQforTiming=renderQ;renderQ=function(){v22PrevRenderQforTiming();v22Enter('TSIA2',state.set&&state.set[state.i])};
const v22PrevRenderSATforTiming=renderSAT;renderSAT=function(){v22PrevRenderSATforTiming();v22Enter('SAT',satState.set&&satState.set[satState.i])};
const v22PrevRenderACTforTiming=renderACT;renderACT=function(){v22PrevRenderACTforTiming();v22Enter('ACT',actState.set&&actState.set[actState.i])};
const v22PrevFinishTestForTiming=finishTest;finishTest=function(auto=false){v22Flush('TSIA2');v22PrevFinishTestForTiming(auto)};

const v22PrevFinishACTForTiming=finishACT;finishACT=function(auto=false){v22Flush('ACT');v22PrevFinishACTForTiming(auto)};

// Rough per-question pacing targets, derived from each section's own real
// time allotment ÷ its real question count (the same numbers used for
// v9AdaptiveStageConfig/actStageConfig above). TSIA2 has no official
// per-question time limit since the real test is untimed/adaptive, so its
// number is a study-pace suggestion, not a derived official limit.
function v22TargetSeconds(examKey,q){
  if(!q)return 75;
  if(examKey==='SAT')return q.section==='Math'?95:71;
  if(examKey==='ACT')return q.section==='Math'?67:q.section==='English'?42:67;
  return 75;
}

// -- mistake-type classification --
// Concept Gap / Process Error / Reading Trap / Pacing-Guess are TSI Practice Prep's
// original four categories; Calculation Error, Misread Question, Formula
// Error, and Careless Mistake extend them with narrower, more actionable
// labels. This is a best-effort heuristic from the signals a static,
// client-only practice tool actually has (time spent, section, skill,
// whether a passage was involved) — a reasonable first-pass diagnosis, not
// a claim of reading the student's mind.
function v22MistakeType(examKey,q,answerIdx,timeSpent){
  if(answerIdx===undefined)return {key:'skipped',label:'Skipped'};
  const isMath=q.section==='Math'||q.section==='Mathematics';
  const isReadingish=/Reading|Craft|Key Ideas|Information|Ideas|ELAR|Text Analysis/i.test((q.section||'')+' '+(q.skill||''));
  const target=v22TargetSeconds(examKey,q);
  if(timeSpent!==null&&timeSpent<Math.max(10,target*0.4))return {key:'pacing',label:'Pacing / Guess'};
  if(q.passage&&isReadingish)return {key:'reading',label:'Reading Trap'};
  if(isMath&&/Geometry|Circle|Triangle|Area|Volume|Trigonometry|Formula/i.test(q.skill||''))return {key:'formula',label:'Formula Error'};
  if(isMath)return {key:'calc',label:'Calculation Error'};
  if(timeSpent!==null&&timeSpent>target*1.8)return {key:'misread',label:'Misread Question'};
  if(q.difficulty==='Easy')return {key:'careless',label:'Careless Mistake'};
  return {key:'concept',label:'Concept Gap'};
}
const V22_FEEDBACK={
  skipped:'You didn’t answer this one — even an educated guess based on elimination beats leaving it blank on the real test.',
  pacing:'You answered this unusually fast for its difficulty. Slow down enough to read every choice before locking in an answer.',
  reading:'The passage likely contained a detail designed to look supportive but not actually match the question. Re-read the exact lines the correct choice points to.',
  formula:'This depends on remembering the right formula. Add it to a formula sheet you review before every practice set.',
  calc:'The setup looks right — this was most likely an arithmetic slip. Redo the computation by hand, one line at a time.',
  misread:'You spent a long time here, which often means the question was misread partway through. Re-read the question stem after solving, before picking an answer.',
  careless:'This is an easier question you know how to do — treat it as a reminder to double-check even the questions that feel automatic.',
  concept:'This points to a gap in the underlying skill rather than a slip. Review the strategy and step-by-step explanation below before trying a similar question.'
};

// -- step-by-step + verification helpers --
// Parses the linear-equation-in-the-question-text pattern several V17/ENR
// families already use ("6x + 3 = 87" style). Shared by both the step-by-step
// derivation and the verification check below so the two stay consistent.
function v22ParseLinearEquation(qtext){
  const m=(qtext||'').match(/([\d.]*)x\s*([+\-−])\s*([\d.]+)\s*=\s*([\d.]+)/);
  if(!m)return null;
  const coefStr=m[1],coef=coefStr?Number(coefStr):1,sign=m[2]==='−'?'-':m[2],b=Number(m[3]),rhs=Number(m[4]);
  if(Number.isNaN(coef)||Number.isNaN(b)||Number.isNaN(rhs))return null;
  return {coefStr,coef,sign,b,rhs};
}
// Parses the "Substitute x=N: f(N)=expr=result" function-evaluation template
// several generated math families use.
function v22ParseFunctionEval(ex){
  const m=(ex||'').match(/f\(([^)]+)\)\s*=\s*(.+?)=\s*(-?[\d.]+)\s*\.?\s*$/);
  if(!m)return null;
  return {arg:m[1].trim(),expr:m[2].trim(),result:m[3].trim()};
}
// Grabs the last standalone number in an explanation string, if any — most
// of the bank's generated ex templates end with the actual computed value.
function v22ExtractFinalNumber(ex){
  const m=(ex||'').match(/(-?[\d.]+)\s*π?\s*\.?\s*$/);
  return m?Number(m[1]):null;
}

// -- Step-by-Step Explanation: real, multi-line derivations instead of one
// compressed sentence, wherever the question's own text/explanation makes
// that possible; otherwise a clean fallback rather than a fabricated one. --
function v22StepByStep(q,correctChoiceText){
  const eq=v22ParseLinearEquation(q.q||'');
  if(eq){
    const xVal=Number(correctChoiceText);
    if(!Number.isNaN(xVal)){
      const afterMove=eq.sign==='+'?eq.rhs-eq.b:eq.rhs+eq.b;
      const coefPart=eq.coefStr||'';
      return [
        `${coefPart}x ${eq.sign} ${eq.b} = ${eq.rhs}`,
        `${coefPart}x = ${afterMove}`,
        `x = ${xVal}`
      ];
    }
  }
  const fn=v22ParseFunctionEval(q.ex||'');
  if(fn){
    return [
      `Substitute x = ${fn.arg} into f(x)`,
      `f(${fn.arg}) = ${fn.expr}`,
      `f(${fn.arg}) = ${fn.result}`
    ];
  }
  // Generic fallback: split the existing explanation into real fragments
  // (sentence/semicolon boundaries, or a colon introducing a computed chain)
  // so even an un-parsed explanation reads as steps rather than one block.
  const raw=(q.ex||'').trim();
  if(raw.includes(':')){
    const [head,...rest]=raw.split(':');
    const tail=rest.join(':').trim();
    if(tail.includes('=')){
      const parts=tail.split('=').map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
      if(parts.length>1){
        return [`${head.trim()}:`, parts[0], ...parts.slice(1).map(p=>`= ${p.replace(/\.$/,'')}`)];
      }
    }
  }
  const fragments=raw.split(/(?<=[.;])\s+/).map(s=>s.trim()).filter(s=>s.length>1);
  if(fragments.length>1)return fragments;
  return [raw];
}

// -- verification / "check your answer" --
// Best-effort: for generated equation-style items, plug the answer back in
// literally; for everything else, give a concrete, skill-appropriate
// checking habit rather than a generic "check your work".
function v22Verification(q,correctChoiceText){
  const skill=q.skill||'',sec=q.section||'';
  const eq=v22ParseLinearEquation(q.q||'');
  if(eq){
    const xVal=Number(correctChoiceText);
    if(!Number.isNaN(xVal)){
      const left=eq.sign==='+'?eq.coef*xVal+eq.b:eq.coef*xVal-eq.b;
      return `Plug x = ${correctChoiceText} back into the original equation: ${eq.coefStr||''}x ${eq.sign} ${eq.b} = ${left} — this should equal ${eq.rhs}.${left===eq.rhs?' ✓ It checks out.':''}`;
    }
  }
  const fn=v22ParseFunctionEval(q.ex||'');
  if(fn)return `Plug x = ${fn.arg} back into f(x): f(${fn.arg}) = ${fn.expr} = ${fn.result} — matches this choice exactly. ✓`;
  const finalNum=v22ExtractFinalNumber(q.ex||''),choiceNum=Number(correctChoiceText);
  if(finalNum!==null&&!Number.isNaN(choiceNum)&&Math.abs(finalNum-choiceNum)<1e-9)
    return `Work back through the steps above: they resolve to ${finalNum}, which matches this choice exactly. ✓`;
  if(/Geometry|Circle|Triangle|Rectangle|Trigonometry|Area|Volume/i.test(skill+' '+sec))return 'Re-derive the answer from the formula with the given numbers, and confirm the units and shape actually match what the question asked for (area vs. perimeter, radius vs. diameter, etc.).';
  if(/Mean|Median|Statistics|Probability|Data/i.test(skill))return 'Recompute the value directly from the listed numbers rather than trusting memory, and confirm every value in the data set was used.';
  if(/Reading|Information|Ideas|Craft|Text Analysis/i.test(skill+' '+sec))return 'Find the exact sentence in the passage that supports the correct choice, and confirm no other choice is also directly supported by the text.';
  if(/Conventions|Grammar|Language|Writing|Editing|Sentence/i.test(skill))return 'Read the completed sentence back to yourself in full — a correct grammar answer should sound natural when read aloud.';
  return 'Re-read the question stem once more and confirm the correct choice actually answers what was asked, not just a true-sounding statement.';
}

// -- Smart Recommendation: one concrete per-question next-step line, tied to
// the specific mistake type and how much recorded practice this skill has. --
function v22Recommendation(skillKey,mistake,hist){
  if(mistake.key==='pacing')return `Recommended Next Step: Redo 2-3 ${skillKey} questions untimed first, focusing on reading every choice before answering.`;
  if(mistake.key==='formula')return `Recommended Next Step: Write the ${skillKey} formula on a reference sheet, then complete 3 more ${skillKey} questions using it.`;
  if(!hist.total||hist.total<4)return `Recommended Next Step: Complete a few more ${skillKey} questions — there's not enough recorded practice yet to tell if this was a one-off.`;
  if(hist.accuracy!==null&&hist.accuracy<60)return `Recommended Next Step: Complete 3 more ${skillKey} questions before moving on to a new skill.`;
  return `Recommended Next Step: Review this question's explanation once more, then try one similar ${skillKey} question to confirm it sticks.`;
}

// -- mastery / previous performance, reusing each exam's own saved history
// (the same skill snapshots already recorded by skillSnapshot/
// attachLatestSkills after every completed test) --
function v22SkillHistory(examKey,skillKey){
  const st=examKey==='SAT'?satStore:examKey==='ACT'?actStore:store;
  // Recorded history is per-session (one aggregated skill snapshot per
  // completed test), not per-individual-question — so a literal "last 5-10
  // questions" window isn't available from this data model. The closest
  // honest approximation: weight the RECENT sessions in this skill rather
  // than an all-time average, so a student's mastery reading updates as
  // their recent performance changes instead of being diluted by a session
  // from weeks ago. Takes the most recent 3 sessions that touched this skill.
  const RECENT_SESSIONS=3;
  const withSkill=(st.history||[]).filter(h=>(h.skills||{})[skillKey]);
  const recent=withSkill.slice(-RECENT_SESSIONS);
  let correct=0,total=0;
  recent.forEach(h=>{const s=h.skills[skillKey];correct+=s.correct||0;total+=s.total||0});
  return {correct,total,accuracy:total?Math.round(correct/total*100):null,sessions:recent.length};
}
function v22MasteryLabel(accuracy,total){
  if(accuracy===null||total<4)return 'Learning';
  if(accuracy<60)return 'Learning';
  if(accuracy<75)return 'Developing';
  if(accuracy>=90&&total>=10)return 'Mastered';
  return 'Proficient';
}

}

function v22ReportIssue(qid){
  const note=prompt('Briefly describe the issue with this question (wrong answer key, typo, unclear wording, etc.):');
  if(note===null)return;
  let log=[];try{log=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('scorepath_reported_issues')||'[]')}catch(e){}
  log.push({qid,note,at:new Date().toISOString()});
  try{localStorage.setItem('scorepath_reported_issues',JSON.stringify(log))}catch(e){}
  const btn=document.getElementById('v22rep-'+qid);
  if(btn){btn.textContent='✓ Reported — thank you';btn.disabled=true}
}
window.v22ReportIssue=v22ReportIssue;

function v22Card(examKey,q,answerIdx,index,total){
  const skipped=answerIdx===undefined,ok=!skipped&&answerIdx===q.a;
  const status=skipped?'skipped':ok?'good':'bad',statusLabel=skipped?'Skipped':ok?'Correct':'Incorrect';
  const yourAnswerHTML=skipped?'<i>No answer selected</i>':`${String.fromCharCode(65+answerIdx)}. ${q.choices[answerIdx]}`;
  const correctText=q.choices[q.a];
  const skillKey=skillGroupKey(q);
  const timeSpent=v22TimeFor(examKey,q.id),target=v22TargetSeconds(examKey,q);
  const mistake=v22MistakeType(examKey,q,answerIdx,timeSpent);
  const hist=v22SkillHistory(examKey,skillKey),masteryLabel=v22MasteryLabel(hist.accuracy,hist.total);
  const cardId=`v22card-${examKey}-${index}`;
  const whyMissed=(!ok&&!skipped&&q.why&&q.why[answerIdx])?`<div class="focusRationale"><b>Why your answer was wrong:</b> ${q.why[answerIdx]}</div>`:'';
  const choiceRows=q.choices.map((c,i)=>{
    const isCorrect=i===q.a,isYours=i===answerIdx,cls=isCorrect?' correctChoice':(isYours&&!isCorrect?' userWrongChoice':'');
    const tag=isCorrect?'<span class="choiceStatus correct">Correct Answer</span>':(isYours?'<span class="choiceStatus yours">Your Answer</span>':'');
    return `<div class="reviewChoice${cls}"><span class="choiceBadge">${String.fromCharCode(65+i)}</span><span>${c}</span>${tag}<div class="reviewRationale">${q.why?.[i]||''}</div></div>`;
  }).join('');
  const timeHTML=timeSpent===null?'':`<div><span>Target Time</span><b>${target}s</b></div><div><span>Your Time</span><b>${timeSpent}s${timeSpent>target*1.3?' ⚠':(timeSpent<target*0.6?' ⚡':'')}</b></div>`;
  const stepsHTML=v22StepByStep(q,correctText).map(line=>`<div class="v22StepLine">${line}</div>`).join('');
  const recommendation=v22Recommendation(skillKey,mistake,hist);
  return `<div class="reviewCard ${status}" id="${cardId}">
   <div class="v22ResultRow"><b class="v22ResultBadge ${status}">${statusLabel}</b><span class="v22Qid">${q.id}</span></div>
   <div class="answerSummary"><div><b>Your Answer</b>${yourAnswerHTML}</div><div class="v22CorrectBox"><b>Correct Answer</b>${String.fromCharCode(65+q.a)}. ${correctText}</div></div>
   ${whyMissed}
   <div class="fullReview"><b>Step-by-Step Explanation</b><div class="v22Steps">${stepsHTML}</div></div>
   <div class="v22Verify"><b>Verification — Check Your Answer</b><p>${v22Verification(q,correctText)}</p></div>
   <div class="fullReview"><b>Choice Analysis</b><div class="fullReviewGrid">${choiceRows}</div></div>
   <div class="strategy"><b>Solution Strategy:</b> ${q.strategy}</div>
   <div class="v22MetaGrid"><div><span>Skill</span><b>${skillKey}</b></div><div><span>Difficulty</span><b>${q.difficulty}</b></div>${timeHTML}</div>
   <div class="v22MistakeBox v22mt-${mistake.key}"><b>Mistake Type: ${mistake.label}</b><p>${V22_FEEDBACK[mistake.key]}</p></div>
   <div class="v22Recommend"><b>${recommendation}</b></div>
   <div class="v22MasteryBox"><div class="v22MasteryTop"><span>${skillKey} Mastery</span><span>${masteryLabel}${hist.total?` • ${hist.accuracy}% (${hist.total} question${hist.total===1?'':'s'})`:''}</span></div><div class="v22MasteryTrack"><i style="width:${Math.max(4,hist.accuracy||0)}%"></i></div>${hist.sessions?`<div class="v22PrevPerf">Recent performance: ${hist.correct} of ${hist.total} correct across your last ${hist.sessions} practice session${hist.sessions===1?'':'s'} in this skill (${hist.accuracy}% accuracy).</div>`:'<div class="v22PrevPerf">No prior recorded practice in this skill yet — this session is your first data point.</div>'}</div>
   <div class="v22Actions">
     <button type="button" class="smallbtn primary2" onclick="v22PracticeSimilar('${examKey}','${skillKey.replace(/'/g,"\\'")}')">🎯 Practice a Similar Question →</button>
     <button type="button" class="smallbtn" id="v22bm-${q.id}" onclick="v22ToggleBookmark('${examKey}','${q.id}')">${(examKey==='SAT'?satStore:examKey==='ACT'?actStore:store).bookmarks.includes(q.id)?'★ Saved for Review':'☆ Save for Review'}</button>
     <button type="button" class="smallbtn" id="v22rep-${q.id}" onclick="v22ReportIssue('${q.id}')">🚩 Report an issue</button>
     <a class="smallbtn" href="#" onclick="const n=document.getElementById('v22card-${examKey}-${index+1}')||document.getElementById('${cardId}');if(n){n.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth',block:'start'})}return false;">${index+1<total?'Next Question ↓':'Back to Top ↑'}</a>
   </div>
  </div>`;
}

// -- Results Dashboard additions: Skipped count + Difficulty Performance,
// appended next to the existing Score/Accuracy/Time/Flagged stat tiles. --
function v22DashboardExtras(examKey,set,answers){
  const skipped=set.filter(q=>answers[q.id]===undefined).length;
  const byDiff={};set.forEach(q=>{const d=q.difficulty||'Medium';if(!byDiff[d])byDiff[d]={c:0,t:0};byDiff[d].t++;if(answers[q.id]===q.a)byDiff[d].c++});
  const diffOrder=['Easy','Medium','Hard'].filter(d=>byDiff[d]);
  const diffHTML=diffOrder.map(d=>{const v=byDiff[d],p=Math.round(v.c/v.t*100);return `<div class="v22DiffRow"><span>${d}</span><div class="v22DiffTrack"><i style="width:${p}%"></i></div><b>${p}% (${v.c}/${v.t})</b></div>`}).join('');
  return {skipped,diffHTML};
}
function v22InjectDashboard(resultsId,statsSelector,examKey,set,answers){
  const results=document.getElementById(resultsId);if(!results)return;
  const stats=results.querySelector(statsSelector);
  const {skipped,diffHTML}=v22DashboardExtras(examKey,set,answers);
  if(stats&&!stats.querySelector('.v22SkippedStat')){
    stats.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend',`<div class="rstat v22SkippedStat"><b>${skipped}</b><span>Skipped</span></div>`);
  }
  let diffBox=results.querySelector('.v22DifficultyBox');
  if(!diffBox){
    diffBox=document.createElement('div');diffBox.className='v22DifficultyBox';
    stats?.insertAdjacentElement('afterend',diffBox);
  }
  diffBox.innerHTML=`<b>Difficulty Performance</b>${diffHTML||'<div class="progressEmpty">No questions to break down.</div>'}`;
}

/* ============================================================
   V23: Monetization — pre-test ad interstitial + a results-screen
   ad zone, both consent-gated and inert until the site owner adds
